title: Tenant spend windowed shaper with region and accelerator affinity
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a tenant-level "windowed shaper" that enforces soft spend windows and burst smoothing across regions and GPU families. The shaper should: (1) maintain a fixed token/compute budget per rolling window (e.g., 1 hour) for each tenant, (2) prefer accelerator families with better unit economics given current spot/on-demand mix, and (3) allow short bursts beyond the window with exponential decay to avoid sudden throttles. This is intended to reduce surprise spend, keep latency SLOs stable by avoiding last-second mass evictions, and provide deterministic fallback behavior to cheaper model variants when near budget exhaustion.
acceptance_criteria:
1) API-level flags to enable windowed shaper per-tenant and a default global policy exist.
2) Router rejects or reroutes requests that would exceed tenant window budget unless marked burst-allowed.
3) Preference scoring returns stable accelerator family choices given live spot prices and recent evictions.
4) Automatic fallback to configured model variants (quantized or smaller family) when remaining window budget falls below 15%.
5) Integration tests covering a simulated tenant with rapid request ramp and spot evictions.
6) Dashboard shows tenant window usage, projected burn rate, and burst debt.
7) No regression in p95 latency beyond 10% for covered tenants in canary region.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: add a Shaper component in the routing tier that maintains in-memory sliding-window counters and a small ML-lite predictor for short-term burn-rate. The Shaper will consult the Cost Oracle (existing service) for live spot/on-demand price signals and an Accelerator Affinity matrix (new data cache) which ranks GPU families by effective cost-per-token and expected preemption risk. Policies are pluggable: soft cap (preferred) returns 429+Retry-After header; hard cap blocks. Fallback variants use existing variant registry; implement weight decay for burst debt to smooth re-entry. Persist per-tenant window configs in Config Store with TTL. Use Redis for counters with local fallback cache for fast decisions.
Trade-offs: consistency vs latency — counters are eventually consistent to avoid routing latency; short inconsistency window may cause minor over-commitment but acceptable within burst decay. Using Redis simplifies rollout but requires careful pipeline to prevent hot keys.
Open questions: exact decay formula for burst debt; default window length (1h vs 15m); whether to expose burst allowance as customer plan feature or keep internal only.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flagged rollout: start with internal tenants and SRE team.
2) Canary region (us-west1) with 5% of traffic from enabled tenants. Monitor cost delta and p95 latency for 72h.
3) Expand to all tenants on dev plane and then opt-in beta customers.
4) After 2 weeks of stable metrics, flip default to enabled for new tenants; existing tenants stay opt-in for one release cycle.
5) Full global rollout tied to release routing-2026.04 and documentation update.
Rollback: disable feature flag and clear burst debt cache.
Migration: migrate existing per-tenant budgets to windowed defaults using historical burn rate analysis.
monitoring_playbook:
Dashboards: tenant-window-usage, per-tenant-burst-debt, accelerator-affinity-distribution, spot-eviction-rate, router-429-rate.
Alerts: if tenant window over-commit > 5% sustained for 15m or router 429 spike > 0.5% baseline.
SRE runbook: On alert, toggle feature flag for the tenant, inspect Redis counters and Cost Oracle health, check affinity ranking anomalies, and contact customer success for high-impact tenants.
Postmortem: if regression in availability or cost, capture decision points and adjust decay formula or default window length.
test_plan: Unit tests for Shaper logic and decay math. Integration test harness simulating: price spikes, spot eviction storms, cross-region failover. Load test with synthetic tenants to validate p50/p95 latency with and without shaper. Canary verification script to validate dashboard metrics and that fallback variants are invoked under low budget. QA checklist includes security review of persisted configs and Redis ACL checks.
